items.title: What is e-Khata
items.answer: e-Khata is the digital property record issued by BBMP for properties in Bengaluru. It digitizes ownership and tax-linked details so records are searchable, verifiable, and easier to update.

items.title: How to apply for e-Khata online
items.answer: Visit https://ekhata.bbmp.gov.in, login with OTP, search property (SAS/PID/owner), review details, upload documents if required, pay official fee, and submit. Track status under My Applications.

items.title: Difference between Draft and Final e-Khata
items.answer: Draft e-Khata is preliminary data from tax/property records and may have incomplete fields. Final e-Khata is verified and legally usable for approvals/transactions after validation and fee payment.

items.title: Difference between e-Khata and New Khata
items.answer: Regular e-Khata usually refers to migration/verification of existing records in BBMP systems. New Khata is for fresh khata creation (for eligible new/unregistered/changed ownership cases). Required documents and scrutiny can differ.
sampleQuestions: difference e khata and new khata
e khata matthu new khata difference

items.title: Why e-Khata is needed
items.answer: e-Khata improves transparency, reduces fraud, supports faster verification, and is increasingly required for civic approvals and property transactions.

items.title: Official e-Khata fees and payment
items.answer: Pay only on official BBMP channels. Charges depend on service type (draft/final/download/application center). Never pay brokers without official receipt.

items.title: How to apply online step-by-step
items.answer: Open BBMP e-Khata portal, authenticate by OTP, choose service, enter property details, upload required docs, pay if applicable, submit, then monitor status online.

items.title: Draft e-Khata missing
items.answer: If draft is missing, re-check SAS/PID/owner spelling, try legacy owner details, and raise grievance from portal with supporting docs for manual verification.

items.title: Non-transactable to transactable Final e-Khata
items.answer: Submit correction/upgrade request with ownership proofs and required validation. BBMP verification is needed before status changes from non-transactable to transactable.

items.title: How to raise grievance
items.answer: Use grievance/help section on portal with application/property reference and clear issue description. Track ticket ID for follow-up.

items.title: What is New Khata
items.answer: New Khata is for fresh khata creation in eligible scenarios where regular e-Khata conversion is not enough. It requires case-specific document validation.

items.title: Property under court order
items.answer: If court order/dispute exists, submission requires legal documents and processing follows legal compliance. Final outcome depends on court directions and BBMP scrutiny.

items.title: Errors in Final e-Khata
items.answer: Raise correction with evidence (sale deed, ID, tax docs, supporting proof). Mention exact wrong fields (name/area/PID/address/share) and submit through official workflow.

items.title: NRI procedure for e-Khata
items.answer: NRI applicants can apply using valid identity/ownership documents and required authorization where applicable. Ensure document consistency and portal-compliant uploads.

items.title: VP/MSB New Khata procedure
items.answer: For VP/MSB category properties, follow the dedicated new khata process and upload category-specific supporting records for verification.

items.title: New Khata for multiple flats or units
items.answer: For multiple units/flats, ensure each unit/owner mapping is clear and submit unit-wise details/documents as required by portal workflow.

items.title: Multiple names clubbed in application
items.answer: Names may be clubbed when records indicate joint/linked ownership. Verify owner shares and supporting docs before requesting split/correction.

items.title: How to file objection to Final e-Khata
items.answer: Use official objection/correction flow, provide property reference and documentary proof, and monitor acknowledgement/ticket status.

items.title: How to apply for New Khata
items.answer: Choose New Khata service in portal, provide property basis and ownership chain, upload mandatory docs, pay official charges, and submit for scrutiny.

items.title: SARFAESI order related e-Khata
items.answer: Where SARFAESI/legal enforcement applies, submission and approval depend on legal records and competent authority instructions.

items.title: What are LPEs
items.answer: LPEs are Local Property Enquiry support points/process touchpoints for property-related assistance as notified by authorities.

items.title: What happens after New Khata application
items.answer: After submission, application goes through scrutiny/verification. You can track status online; if query is raised, upload additional documents promptly.

items.title: Official portal URL and safety
items.answer: Use only official BBMP e-Khata portal: https://ekhata.bbmp.gov.in. Avoid look-alike sites and never share OTP outside official flow.

items.title: Documents generally needed
items.answer: Typical docs: identity proof, ownership proof (sale deed/registered docs), property tax references (SAS/PID), and case-specific supporting files as required.

items.title: Handle mixed-language noisy user query
items.answer: Interpret intent first, then answer in detected user language. If still ambiguous, ask one short clarification between two likely intents.

items.title: Avoid overconfident legal claims
items.answer: If exact clause/timeline is uncertain, state that it is case-dependent and advise user to check latest status through official portal or grievance desk.

items.title: Video suggestion policy
items.answer: When intent matches a known topic, suggest only one best-fit YouTube tutorial link and avoid repeating the same link multiple times in one answer.

items.title: Disambiguate similar difference questions
items.answer: When user says only 'difference', first infer from context. If context is weak, ask: Do you mean Draft vs Final e-Khata or e-Khata vs New Khata?
